rules_text:
Rules summary Overview This is a Co-operative game of clue giving and deduction Turn On your turn, you can either play a card or guess a card When playing a card, orientation matters, the side facing the middle of the table contains the information you wish to provide When playing a card, you are trying to give information about the rest of your hand, when a played card is no longer true about your hand it is moved to Agony The sides of the cards are all the same, with the following hints (3 colour hints, and 1 number hint), Highest colour, Lowest colour, Final colour, More Number Alternatively to playing a card, you can guess a card in another player's hand using their hints. If you are correct, the guessed card goes to their Harmony and you can put any one of your hand cards into Harmony too, so each of you add to Harmony for a total of 2 cards added. If you are incorrect, wherever the guessed card actually is, that player adds it to Agony, and the guesser adds a hand card of their choice into Agony, however if the card does not exist in someone's hand then only the incorrect guesser adds a card to Agony, as such 1-2 cards will be added to Agony in this way. Game End Depending on player count, the game ends after a set number of rounds. When the final round is over, players add their played hint cards as well as hand cards into Agony if Harmony is higher than Agony, the players win! However, if Agony contains more cards than Harmony, the players lose!

---

[Rating: 3/10] Bought based on reviews, but we didn't find it fun--or even much of a game. We passed it on after one play. Others might enjoy it as intended--or just want a deck of 5 suits numbered through 10. Below are my pre-play notes:  Misleading name. We'd prefer one quality storage box instead of a flimsy tuck box inside of an oversized box w/ plastic insert. Hard Mode seems to increase the hidden information rather than challenging players more fairly. So after learning and practicing, we may find it lacks variability.  Otherwise looks like a good limited communication deduction puzzle for the price. 

[Rating: 3/10] I wanted to like this game, but in practice there just isn't enough information to be fun. I liked the idea of a pared-down Bomb Busters, but there just wasn't enough to go on and players became frustrated.

[Rating: 4/10] Why even put 2 player count on the box? You need to play 'Go fish' if you want even a slight chance of winning at that player count. The designer said "we have been workshopping 2P as it is a weakness of the game." No kidding Sherlock! Maybe do a little bit more developing before publishing the game? Truly a barn made game...

[Rating: 5/10] I like deduction games in general and might well like this if the rules were re-written. As it stands a crucial rule - discarding relevant cards - is included as if it were an afterthought, and is not explained at all. The explanations offered in the forums here help but are not sufficient.

[Rating: 5/10] A cooperative game where you are trying to guess all the cards in everyone's hand before the game timer runs out.  It has the limited communication element that I like, similar to The Crew.  You need to make some blind guesses sometimes in order to try to win.  I think 3 players is the sweet spot for this game.

[Rating: 5/10] Cooperative deduction game. Similar to Hanabi except your cards are facing towards you and you are trying to convey to others what is in your hand. Because the clues you can give are entirely tied to what cards are in your hand, it feels a lot more restrictive than other, similar games. It leaves players in awkward spots, regularly, where they have nothing productive to do with their turn, but also no clues with which to make a guess. This is especially true at 2 players. Expressions is fine and does what it sets out to do, I just think there are better choices for this type of game.
